readme:
# Eventbrite Scraper - Events & Conferences

Scrape event data from [Eventbrite](https://www.eventbrite.com), the world's largest event platform with millions of events in 180+ countries.

> **Integration stopped on Nov 11?** After a security incident, Apify rotated the API tokens of affected accounts. If yours was rotated and you call this Actor from n8n, Make, Zapier or your own code, paste your new token (Console → Settings → API & Integrations). Schedules inside Apify were not affected.

## What data can you extract?

- **Event details**: title, description, start/end dates, timezone
- **Venue info**: name, full address, city, country, GPS coordinates
- **Pricing**: ticket price, currency, free/paid status
- **Organizer**: name, profile URL, verified badge, total attendees and events hosted
- **Availability**: sales status, sold-out and cancelled flags, sales end date, numeric min/max price
- **Full description** as plain text
- **Categories & tags**: event category and tags
- **Media**: event image URL

## Use with AI Agents (MCP)

Connect this actor to any MCP-compatible AI client — Claude Desktop, Claude.ai, Cursor, VS Code, LangChain, LlamaIndex, or custom agents.

**Apify MCP server URL:**

```
https://mcp.apify.com?tools=santamaria-automations/eventbrite-scraper
```

**Example prompt once connected:**

> "Use `eventbrite-scraper` to scrape tech events in Berlin from Eventbrite. Return results as a table."

Clients that support dynamic tool discovery (Claude.ai, VS Code) will receive the full input schema automatically via `add-actor`.

## How to use

### Option 1: Search URLs

Paste any Eventbrite search URL directly:

```json
{
  "searchUrls": [
    "https://www.eventbrite.com/d/germany/tech/",
    "https://www.eventbrite.com/d/ca--san-francisco/conferences/"
  ],
  "maxResults": 100
}
```

### Option 2: Search query + location

```json
{
  "searchQuery": "tech",
  "location": "germany",
  "maxResults": 50
}
```

### Location format

Eventbrite uses URL slugs for locations:
- Countries: `germany`, `united-states`, `france`
- Regions: `united-states--new-york`, `germany--berlin`
- Cities: `ca--san-francisco`, `united-kingdom--london`
- Online: `online`

The category part of a URL is a slug such as `tech`, `music`, `conferences` or `all-events`. The bare `events` slug has no listing data, so it is mapped to `all-events` automatically.

## Input parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `searchUrls` | string[] | - | Eventbrite search page URLs |
| `searchQuery` | string | - | Search keyword |
| `location` | string | `germany` | Location slug for URL building |
| `maxResults` | integer | 100 | Maximum events to scrape in total (1-5000). Since 1.2 the budget is shared across all `searchUrls`: each URL gets an even share and unused results roll over to the next URL. |
| `includeDetails` | boolean | `true` | Fetch each event's detail page for price, currency and organizer. Turn off for a faster run |

### Extra fields

- From the search page: `language`, `published_at`, `series_id`, `urgency_signals` (goingFast, fewTickets, salesEndSoon), `venue_postal_code`, `venue_region`.
- From the event page (with `includeDetails`): `subcategory`, `event_format`, `location_type`, `duration_minutes`, `age_restriction`, `door_time`, `parking`, `refund_policy`, `sales_start_date`, organizer `organizer_id` / `organizer_logo_url` / `organizer_description` / `organizer_hosting_since_years`, the speaker lineup `performers` (name, tagline, role, bio, image, social links), `faq` and `video_urls`.
- Organizer contact data (with `includeDetails`): `organizer_email`, `organizer_phone`, `contact_emails` and `organizer_social_links`. Eventbrite has no structured organizer email or phone field, so these come from addresses and links organizers type into their organizer profile text or event description. Events without a shown address return `null` / `[]`; contact forms are not followed. Phone numbers are only taken when announced by a keyword (Tel, Phone, Mobile ...) or a `tel:` link.

## Performance

- 128 MB memory is enough (Go binary with TLS fingerprinting, peak about 25 MB)
- ~20 events per search page
- Fetches detail pages for price and organizer data (switch off with `includeDetails: false`)
- Eventbrite serves at most 49 pages (about 1,000 events) per search, so split large pulls across several cities or categories
- Empty input scrapes up to 10 events in Germany (demo run)
- Built-in proxy handling, nothing to configure

`attendee_count` is always `null`: Eventbrite does not publish how many people registered for an event. `sales_status`, `is_sold_out` and the organizer totals are the closest honest signals. The new availability and organizer fields need `includeDetails` (default on).

## Pricing

Pay per result: $0.003 per event extracted.


## FAQ

**Do I need a proxy or an Eventbrite login?**
No login. Proxy handling is built in, nothing to configure.

**How many Eventbrite events can I get per run?**
Up to 5,000 per run via `maxResults`. Eventbrite serves at most 49 pages (about 1,000 events) per search, so split large pulls across several cities or categories.

**How fresh is the data?**
Each run reads the live Eventbrite pages, so results reflect what Eventbrite shows at run time. `scraped_at` records the time.

**Why is `attendee_count` null?**
Eventbrite does not publish registration counts. Use `sales_status` and `is_sold_out` instead.

**Can I get events from one city or category?**
Yes. Use a location slug such as `germany--berlin` with a `searchQuery` such as `tech`, or paste an Eventbrite search URL.
